metadata.title: An Extended Dataset of Educational Quality Across Countries (1970–2023)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This paper is a cross-country dataset construction and harmonization study rather than a student-level ILSA microdata analysis. It does not estimate student achievement models with ILSA sampling weights; instead, it constructs harmonized country-year test-score series and imputes missing country-year observations. Because the dependent quantities are country-level harmonized scores and derived educational quality indexes (including working-age indexes using population weights), survey-weight variables from PISA/TIMSS are not applicable in the ML training stage described. The only explicit weighting mentioned is population weighting in the construction of the 15–19 educational quality series and the working-age educational quality index (15–64), not complex survey sampling weights.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The study does not analyze student-level cognitive achievement plausible values (PVs) from PISA/TIMSS; instead, it harmonizes and imputes country-year test-score indicators and then derives educational quality indexes. As a result, PV-based missing-data handling is not applicable to the constructed dataset. Missingness is addressed via linear interpolation and LASSO-based prediction for country-year observations, but the paper does not frame this as a PV/multiple-imputation procedure with a standard missing-data-handling label for PVs.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The dataset covers 101 countries with observations spanning 1970–2023, using 12 assessment years (1970, 1980, 1984, 1990, 1995, 1999, 2003, 2007, 2011, 2015, 2019, 2023). It uses TIMSS as the reference metric by anchoring all harmonized scores to the TIMSS 1995 scale (mean=500, SD=100) and mapping PISA scores via equi-percentile linking. It incorporates earlier IEA/IAEP assessments (First International Science Study 1970–1972; Second International Mathematics Study 1980–1982; Second International Science Study 1983–1984; and IAEP/NCES 1988 and 1990–1991). The final country set excludes countries lacking nationally representative samples (explicitly including China and India) and excludes country-years where key World Bank education/economic indicators are missing, which are required to build the predictor set for LASSO imputation. The analytic panel is constructed as a balanced 101-country × 12-year grid (1212 potential country-year observations), with 631 observed points and 581 missing points imputed using interpolation (Tscore_INT) and LASSO prediction (Tscore_ML).

main_findings.dataset_used: Harmonized cross-country test scores (TIMSS 1995 scale; 1970–2023; country-year panel)
main_findings.target_variable: Tscore_ML (harmonized test scores imputed via LASSO)
main_findings.performance_metrics: LASSO imputation model — RMSE: 17.5, R²: 0.912 (with 80% training / 20% validation and grid search with 10-fold cross-validation); out-of-sample RMSE: 15.7, R²: 0.905; agreement between interpolation and LASSO estimates: correlation = 0.967
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using the harmonized cross-country test-score panel (TIMSS 1995 scale; 1970–2023) the study leveraged World Bank education/economic indicators to predict missing harmonized test scores via LASSO, finding that the LASSO model achieved strong predictive accuracy (RMSE=17.5, R²=0.912; out-of-sample RMSE=15.7, R²=0.905) and produced highly consistent imputations relative to linear interpolation (correlation=0.967). This indicates that data-driven imputation using economic and educational covariates can substantially extend cross-country educational quality time series where direct TIMSS/PISA observations are sparse, enabling more comprehensive inequality and human-capital research.

data.outcome_summary: This paper constructs an extended cross-country dataset of educational quality for 101 countries from 1970 to 2023 by harmonizing mathematics and science test scores from TIMSS, PISA, and earlier IEA/IAEP assessments onto the TIMSS 1995 metric (mean=500, SD=100). It then imputes missing country-year observations (48% missing; 581 of 1212 potential) using two approaches: linear interpolation/extrapolation (Tscore_INT) and a machine-learning prediction model based on LASSO regression (Tscore_ML) trained on 501 fully observed World Bank education and economic indicators. Model selection uses an 80/20 train/validation split with grid search and 10-fold cross-validation, yielding RMSE=17.5 and R²=0.912 (out-of-sample RMSE=15.7, R²=0.905). The two imputation methods agree closely (correlation=0.967), and the dataset further derives annual 15–19 educational quality indicators and working-age (15–64) quality indexes using population weights and an assumed return to test-score gains. Because this is a dataset construction study (not student-level PV modeling), results should be interpreted as imputation accuracy for harmonized country-year indicators rather than causal effects on individual achievement.
